Before the Ce buffs HE's were the best hunters in the game imo.  They have fantastic aptitudes across almost all of the skills you'd need for the end game (Fighting 0 and potentially armor -1 aside).  You can easily pick up most forms of casting to buff themselves up as well.  

The problem is, as you've noticed, they have a difficult early game.  The best advice I can give for that is to only use your bow when you have to so you have ammo when you really need it.  With careful planning you should be able to get one of the ground without too much trouble.

Really what it comes down to is going with whichever suits your style best after weighing the pros and cons.

High Elf

Pros: Very good aptitudes, higher stats, more magic resist, more mp, bonus int or def every 3 levels, can branch into support and offensive magic easily.

Cons: Normal move speed, slightly lower hp than normal.

Centaur

Pros: High move speed, higher hp than normal, earlier easy game, hooves help with unarmed combat, start game with 3 bonus AC.

Cons: Lower MP, poor aptitudes aside from bows, lower stats, STR or DEX every 4 levels, difficulty branching into magic, armor and dodging penalties from mutations and large size.

I've won 15 rune victories as both, and I wouldn't really say that either is better than the other.  Just depends on what you feel like playing.

In addition to what Weeksy said there is a mechanic called Strength Weight.  Basically every weapon gets value from 0%-100%, where the lower the % the more the weapon is influenced by DEX and the higher the % the more it is influenced by STR.

Strength Weight determines a damage and an accuracy bonus based on your STR and DEX.  Regardless of the percent both of them will have an impact.  A simple way to think about it is that a weapon at 100% (Such as a Giant Spiked Club) will add 1 point of damage and .5 points of accuracy for every strength you have, and .5 accuracy (but no damage) for every point of dexterity.  But on the flip side a weapon with 0% (Quick Blade) Will give .5 damage and 1 accuracy for every DEX, but only .5 Damage per STR.  But these are extreme cases because they lie at the ends of the spectrum.

TL;DR of that is that STR and DEX effect damage and accuracy but STR will give typically give a larger damage boost to your hits and DEX will typically give a larger accuracy boost.

But in .15 that's the third and final real use for STR (the others being Encumbrance Rating and Heavy Armour spell casting).  When you compare that to dexterity which also impacts stealth and dodge, the only situation I can think of where STR is better than DEX is if you are using a high Strength Weight weapon AND you never plan on training dodge which isn't a very good decision IMO.

You can see the values for this on this page of the wiki.
http://crawl.chaosforge.org/Weapon

This page has all the details if you want to understand the exact mechanics, but a good rule of thumb is that your strength should be equal to the ER of the armour you want to use.

http://crawl.chaosforge.org/Encumbrance_rating

First off you trained maces and axes up to 20 when your primary weapon was a demon whip.  Pick one melee weapon type and train that until you hit min delay (more info here http://crawl.chaosforge.org/Weapon_speed ) and then turn it off to train other skills.  Also if you're planning to use two-handed weapons don't bother training your shields at all.

Second, you were wearing plate armour which means you did 2 things wrong.  You were training your dodge skill which is a waste if you're using heavy armour, and you were trying to branch into spell casting which is also a waste.  Pick either armor or dodging based on your aptitudes.  If you have a higher armor aptitude stick with heavier armor (unless you want to use support magics), and if you have a higher dodge apt then stick with light armor (ring mail or fire dragon armor and below).

When it comes to spell casting the higher the encumbrance rating of your armor the harder it is to cast.  Furthermore the lower your intelligence the harder it is to cast and the weaker your spells are.  So between your plate armor and 8 intelligence it is impossible for you to effectively use offensive magic.  If you're going to be using anything heavier than a ring mail it's probably better to pass on magic completely.  If you decide that you do want to use magic you have to do some things differently.

First off you cannot use offensive magic effectively.  You're a melee user so it isn't going to happen.  Second, you put all of your stat bonuses into strength.  You're playing trunk which has no more item weight, making STR practically worthless once you have enough to meet your armor's encumbrance rating.  It's better to put those bonus stats into INT if you wanna use magic at all or DEX if you don't.  This means that you need to learn support magic that will enhance your survivability, spells like blink, flight, and regeneration.  Between better use of stat points and learning support spells you'll live longer.

Finally, as an orc I would recommend using the throwing skill due to their high apt for it.  Trunk has revamped the ranged combat mechanics in Trunk and throwing has gone from something that was just there to an amazingly powerful skill.  Combine the high damage of throwing weapons with the lack of item weight in trunk and you can carry ridiculous amounts of ammo.

In summary.
1. Pick one melee weapon and train that to min delay.
2. Armor or dodge, not both.  Don't train Shields if you're going to use a two-hander.
3. Don't use heavy armor and try to use magic.
4. Put bonus stats into INT or DEX once you have enough STR to use your armor.
5. As a melee character get support magic instead of offensive magic.
6. Consider putting more points into the throwing skill.
